new_entities.name: Acupuncture for migraine prophylaxis
new_entities.description: Acupuncture administered preventively to reduce future migraine burden.

new_entities.name: Migraine frequency
new_entities.description: How often migraine attacks or migraine days occur over time.

edges.effect_quant: A 2021 trial-sequential meta-analysis of 20 studies and 3,380 participants found acupuncture superior to sham for migraine episodes after treatment (SMD -0.29, 95% CI -0.47 to -0.11), while a Cochrane review of 22 trials and 4,419 participants found higher response rates and fewer headaches than no prophylactic treatment or routine care.
edges.population: adults receiving acupuncture to prevent recurrent migraine, especially episodic migraine without aura
edges.mechanism: Preventive acupuncture may alter pain modulation, autonomic balance, and attack susceptibility over time, though the magnitude of benefit is modest and protocol-dependent.
edges.summary: For migraine prevention, acupuncture has a reasonably consistent preventive signal. The effect is not huge, but pooled evidence supports fewer migraine episodes than sham or no prophylaxis in many trial settings.
edges.caveats: The effect size is modest and should be framed as one preventive option rather than a universally superior therapy. Comparator choice matters, and not every trial has shown clear superiority over active drug prophylaxis.

evidence.citation: Fan SQ et al 2021 J Neurol
evidence.notes: Efficacy of acupuncture for migraine prophylaxis: a trial sequential meta-analysis.

evidence.citation: Linde K et al 2009 Cochrane Database Syst Rev

evidence.notes: Acupuncture in migraine prevention: a randomized sham controlled study with 6-months posttreatment follow-up.
